Hi Jared / Priya �14

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your customer-led load test scheduled:

Recap (from today's discovery)
- SLO targets: p95 latency <= 400ms for streaming responses; p95 <= 300ms for non-streaming completions.
- Throughput target: sustained 300 requests/minute during peak window.
- Concurrency: expect up to 60 concurrent active sessions (session = 1 streaming connection).
- Streaming: requires chunked responses with keep-alive; client will validate partial tokens and reorder handling.
- Auth: tests will use test API keys (scoped to test project) and a separate test account set.

Proposed next steps
1) We share a k6 script and a short Locust example for the test flows (attached: k6-acme-loadtest-v1.js).
2) You provide a 2-hour window for the customer-led run and an IP allowlist so we can allow traffic from your test runners (we've asked ops to prepare acme-ip-allowlist.csv format below).
3) We will provision test API keys & a low-privilege test account (credentials attached as acme-test-accounts.txt stub).
4) Engineering (cc: Aditya) will confirm risks and any KV-cache resets we should be aware of and provide guidance on warm-up ramps.

Proposed test window: Thu Feb 18, 10:00-12:00 PST (happy to adjust). Please confirm the window and the public IPs you will run from.

Attachments: k6-acme-loadtest-v1.js (script stub), acme-test-accounts.txt (credentials stub), acme-ip-allowlist.csv (example format).

If that's all good I'll get the test keys and allowlist in place and post the short runbook to the Drive folder.

Thanks — quick tech notes from infra for the run:

1) QPS / throttles
- We'll provision a test API key with a soft cap of 600 QPS and a per-minute quota to match your 300 req/min target. That should allow headroom for short bursts.

2) Suggested k6/Locust parameters (what we recommend you run)
- k6: ramp-up 10m to 60 VUs, sustained 2h steady state at ~60 VUs; vus perform a mix of streaming (60%) and non-streaming (40%) flows.
- For streaming flows use websocket/keep-alive connections with an average session duration of 90s and periodic chunk reads — we included an example in k6-acme-loadtest-v1.js.
- Locust: spawn rate 1 user/sec up to 60 users if you prefer.

3) KV cache / warming
- Please run a 15-minute warm-up at 20% traffic 30 minutes prior to the main window to populate caches.
- We'll perform a KV cache flush on the model instance 35 minutes prior (Aditya action). Avoid running the main test during any other scheduled job.

4) Observability & data collection
- We'll enable a high-resolution trace during the window and provide per-token latency breakdowns (p50/p95/p99) within 24 hours.
- If you want token-level logs we need to enable a retention flag; please confirm if you need that (might incur small storage cost).

5) Allowlist and endpoints
- Endpoint to test: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/acme/infer (streaming and non-streaming paths supported).
- IPs must be provided in CSV column ip_address and we will add to allowlist 48 hours before the run.

Let me know if any of this is blocking. I'll schedule the cache flush and key provisioning once we have the IPs from Priya.

-Aditya
